offers_products.reason: It sells correctional facility management, rehabilitation and monitoring services. It sells no goods or software as a main offering.

offers_services.reason: Runs secure facilities, reentry centers, rehabilitation programs, healthcare and electronic monitoring for government partners.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Government agencies choose and pay for detention and reentry services. The individuals in custody do not choose them.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Customers are government agencies, including federal, state and international correctional and immigration authorities.

recurring_revenue.reason: Multi-year government contracts pay daily per-diem rates for occupied beds and monitoring, so revenue repeats.

cyclical_demand.reason: Government corrections, detention and reentry contracts are mandated and keep going when the economy turns down.

big_ticket.reason: Government agencies pay daily per-diem rates for custody and monitoring; sales are small, frequent and ongoing.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue depends on owned and operated detention facilities and beds. Staff matter, but the facilities are the main asset.

large_customers.reason: Main customers are federal, state and foreign government agencies, such as ICE, the US Marshals and state corrections departments.

asset_heavy.reason: Owns and operates roughly 76,000 beds across secure facilities, processing centers and reentry centers; needs ongoing property investment.

notes: Company also has electronic monitoring and facility development, but these are smaller than secure facility management.
